items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: And I was lucky enough to play with that man.

ctx.x: name of (unintelligible) in Brazil was the more outstanding, to me, piano player that I have heard today. And I hate to say this. When the people talk about Perrochin, they talk about Leelee, it's because they never heard Benito, because if you have ever heard Benito, (unintelligible), you're going to find out how hard these people tried to copy. They never got into what Benito used to do.

And I was lucky enough to play with that man. And one later book that they released, for the first time I seen the picture of Benito. He died in Brazil -- went to Brazil at the end of the '30s. He died there. To me, he was one of the greatest true piano players that ever put his hands on a piano. And I thought (unintelligible) was the classic.

I'd like to move on to some individuals to happen in this country, well known -- people who were well known, and have you talk a bit about your feelings on their music, the good side and the bad side (inaudible) and so on.
